questions.text: If $A=\{1,2,3,4\}$, find the power set of $A$.
If $a:b=c:d=e:f$, show that $\dfrac{a^2b+c^2d+e^2f}{ab^2+cd^2+ef^2}=\dfrac{a+c+e}{b+d+f}$.
Solve the equation using the componendo-dividendo theorem: $\dfrac{(x+3)^2+(x-1)^2}{(x+3)^2-(x-1)^2}=\dfrac{5}{4}$.
If $a:b=c:d=e:f$, show that $\dfrac{a^4b^2+a^2e^2-e^4f}{b^6+b^2f^2-f^5}=\dfrac{a^4}{b^4}$.
Find the inverse of the matrix by the adjoint method: $A=\begin{bmatrix}1&0&1\\-4&1&-1\\6&-2&1\end{bmatrix}$.
Find the inverse of the matrix $A=\begin{bmatrix}2&1&1\\3&2&1\\2&1&2\end{bmatrix}$ by the adjoint method.
Find the inverse of the matrix $A=\begin{bmatrix}1&0&1\\-4&1&-1\\6&-2&1\end{bmatrix}$ by the adjoint method.
Find the value of $m$ if the roots of the equation $x^2-5x+2m=0$ differ by $1$.
Find all the cube roots of $-125$.
If $\alpha,\beta$ are the roots of the equation $px^2+qx+q=0$, $p\ne0$, find the value of $\sqrt{\dfrac{\alpha}{\beta}}+\sqrt{\dfrac{\beta}{\alpha}}$.
Resolve $\dfrac{11-3x}{(x-1)(x+3)}$ into partial fractions.
Resolve $\dfrac{4x-3}{(x+1)^2}$ into partial fractions.
Resolve $\dfrac{4(x-4)}{x^2-2x-3}$ into partial fractions.

The marks obtained by students in a subject (out of $50$) are given in the following grouped table. Find the mode. Marks: $25$–$29$, $30$–$34$, $35$–$39$, $40$–$44$, $45$–$49$; numbers of students: $9,18,35,17,5$.
Find the variance of the numbers of absentees in a class for the last seven days: $3,5,3,2,4,1,8$.

The following data show the number of devices resulting in observation values in appropriate ranges. Find the harmonic mean (H.M.). Class limits: $10.5$–$10.9$, $11.0$–$11.4$, $11.5$–$11.9$, $12.0$–$12.4$, $12.5$–$12.9$; frequencies: $2,7,10,12,8$.
Find the mean deviation of the marks of students: $4,7,12,76,48,4,51$.

The marks obtained by students in a subject (out of $50$) are given in the following grouped table. Find the arithmetic mean (A.M.). Marks: $25$–$29$, $30$–$34$, $35$–$39$, $40$–$44$, $45$–$49$; numbers of students: $9,18,35,17,5$.
Find the standard deviation (S.D.) of the marks of students: $90,30,85,50,25$.
In a right-angled triangle, the square of the length of the hypotenuse is equal to the sum of the squares of the lengths of the other two sides. Prove it.
If the square of one side of a triangle is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two sides, then the triangle is a right-angled triangle. Prove it.
In a right-angled triangle, the square of the length of the hypotenuse is equal to the sum of the squares of the lengths of the other two sides. Prove it.
If two triangles are similar, the measures of their corresponding sides are proportional. Prove it.
The internal bisector of an angle of a triangle divides the opposite side in the ratio of the sides containing the angle. Prove it.
A line parallel to one side of a triangle and intersecting the other two sides divides them proportionally. Prove it.
If a line segment intersects two sides of a triangle in the same ratio, then it is parallel to the third side. Prove it.
If two chords of a circle are congruent, then they are equidistant from the centre. Prove it.
A straight line drawn from the centre of a circle to bisect a chord (which is not a diameter) is perpendicular to the chord. Prove it.
A straight line drawn from the centre of a circle to bisect a chord (which is not a diameter) is perpendicular to the chord. Prove it.
If two circles touch internally, the distance between their centres is equal to the difference of their radii. Prove it.
If two circles touch externally, the distance between their centres is equal to the sum of their radii. Prove it.
If a line is drawn perpendicular to a radial segment of a circle at its outer endpoint, it is tangent to the circle at that point. Prove it.
If two circles touch internally, the distance between their centres is equal to the difference of their radii. Prove it.
If a line is drawn perpendicular to a radial segment of a circle at its outer endpoint, it is tangent to the circle at that point. Prove it.
If the angles subtended by two chords of a circle (or congruent circles) at the centres (corresponding centres) are equal, the chords are equal. Prove it.
If two arcs of a circle are congruent, then the corresponding chords are equal. Prove it.
If two chords of a circle (or of congruent circles) are equal, then their corresponding arcs (minor, major or semicircle) are congruent. Prove it.
If two arcs of a circle (or congruent circles) are congruent, then the corresponding chords are equal. Prove it.

questions.chapter: 28: Angle in a Segment of a Circle
questions.text: Any two angles in the same segment of a circle are equal. Prove it.

questions.chapter: 28: Angle in a Segment of a Circle
questions.text: The central angle of a minor arc is double the measure of the inscribed angle of the corresponding major arc. Prove it.
Draw the inscribed circle of $\triangle ABC$ in which $\overline{AB}=7\,\mathrm{cm}$, $\angle B=60^\circ$ and $\overline{BC}=6\,\mathrm{cm}$. Also write the steps of construction.
Draw the circumcircle of $\triangle ABC$ in which $\overline{AB}=5.5\,\mathrm{cm}$, $\overline{AC}=6\,\mathrm{cm}$ and $\angle A=60^\circ$. Also write the steps of construction.

Draw two unequal circles of radii $3.4\,\mathrm{cm}$ and $2.1\,\mathrm{cm}$ with centres $A$ and $B$, respectively, such that $\overline{AB}=7.5\,\mathrm{cm}$. Draw direct common tangents to these circles. Also write the steps of construction.
Prove that $\sqrt{\dfrac{1+\cos\theta}{1-\cos\theta}}=\dfrac{\sin\theta}{1-\cos\theta}$, where $\cos\theta\ne1$.
A ladder makes an angle of $60^\circ$ with the ground and reaches a height of $6\,\mathrm{cm}$ on the wall. Find the length of the ladder.
Find the remaining trigonometric functions if $\sin\theta=\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ and $\theta$ lies in the second quadrant.
Prove that $\sin^2\theta=\dfrac{\tan^2\theta}{1+\tan^2\theta}$.
Prove that $\dfrac{\cot\theta+\csc\theta}{\sin\theta+\tan\theta}=\csc\theta\cot\theta$.
A ladder makes an angle of $60^\circ$ with the ground and reaches a height of $6\,\mathrm{m}$ on the wall. Find the length of the ladder.
